requirement:
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST author the evidence of one existing requirement or named example in the
current project, under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
rationale:
The implementation covers the invocation obligations. One obligation lacks a test that asserts its outcome: in the default mode, the report must identify the evidence-file path.

**Obligations and the code that carries them out**
- **Command form and alias.** `src/main.rs` `Command::Author` defines the `author` command, its `author-evidence` alias, `--config`, `--missing`/`--force`, `--stdout` and `-v/--verbose`. `--missing` conflicts with `--force` and `--stdout`, and a subject conflicts with `--all`.
- **Author one existing subject under refresh.** `AuthoringSubject::parse`, `author_evidence_with_options` and `configured_assessment` in `src/authoring/mod.rs` do this, along with `AssessmentSources::prepare` in `src/authoring/inputs.rs`. `prepare` rejects a name that is not a requirement or example with "no matching requirement or named example". `author_evidence_with_options` returns early when the evidence is current (`batch::subject_is_current`) and sets `force` when `--stdout` is selected.
- **Report subject, backend, model, evidence destination and usage-record path.** The single-subject branch of `main` prints `"{subject}: {backend} / {model}; policy …"`, then `Evidence: <path>` and `Usage: <path>`.
- **Evidence destination.** `configured_assessment` returns `Some(path)` for file output and `None` for stdout. `main` prints the file path in the first case and `Evidence: stdout` in the second.
- **Stdout mode sends the report and diagnostics to stderr.** `main` uses `eprintln!` for the report and for the "false" diagnostics in stdout mode. Errors propagate out of `main` and are written to stderr.

**Tests that cover these**
- `stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files` runs `author-evidence --stdout`. It asserts the report on stderr (`{SUBJECT}: ollama / {MODEL}`, `Evidence: stdout`, a `Usage:` path that exists) and the false/FIXME diagnostics on stderr.
- It also asserts the alias, and `missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject` covers `--stdout` implying `--force`.
- `author_rejects_unknown_subjects_and_conflicting_targets` covers the unknown subject and the conflicting-flag errors.
- `missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject` covers `--missing`, `--force`, their exclusivity and the current-record skip.
- The verbose and Ollama CLI tests run the default mode.

**Gap: the default-mode evidence path is not asserted**
The requirement says the evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by default. The default-mode tests only check that stdout contains the label `Evidence:` and `Usage:`.
- `ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free` also checks that stdout contains the model.
- `verbose_single_author_reports_only_false_rationale_without_source_inputs` checks only the two labels.
- I searched `tests/` for `Evidence:` and for the path being printed. No test asserts that the printed value is the evidence-file path (`evidence/<subject>.json`), or that the default-mode report names the subject and backend.

The only assertion on the evidence value is `Evidence: stdout` in stdout mode. The file-path branch in `src/main.rs` prints `path.display()` and has its own conditional. A bug printing the wrong path would pass every current test. The file-path branch is neither a pass-through nor a case that needs network access or process-wide state, so no exemption applies.

There are no `{fixme}` references to acknowledge this gap, so it is unacknowledged.

text: :::{req} invocation
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST author the evidence of one existing requirement or named example in the
current project, under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
:::{req} refresh
Every `habeas author` form MUST accept `--missing` and `--force`, which are
mutually exclusive; `--missing` MUST be the default. Under `--missing`, the
command MUST assess only the selected subjects whose evidence is missing, stale,
or invalid, and MUST preserve every current record without invoking a model,
including accepted FIXME judgments and current false judgments; a current false
judgment is reassessed only when its subject or inputs change or `--force` is
given. Under `--force`, the command MUST assess every selected subject. `--stdout`
MUST imply `--force`, because it writes no evidence. The command MUST report the
number of selected subjects it skipped as current. When no assessment is needed,
the command MUST succeed without resolving model configuration or credentials.
